course_title: Freshman Seminar: Jews & Other Others in the US
subject: JS
requirement_designation: First Year Seminar with Race & Ethnicity(*)
requirements: First Year Seminar with Race & Ethnicity(*)
course_description: Designed to engage first-year students in aspects of inquiry and research into areas of Jewish religion, culture, history, or language. Topics will vary.
course_notes: (Same as HIST 190 3) (Freshmen Seminar - Limited to First Year Students Only) (This course will explore Jews' place in America's diverse ethnic and racial mix. We will compare the history and experiences of Jews in the U.S. to those of African Americans, Asian Americans, Latinos, and European ethnic groups, and will also consider how Jewishness has often overlapped with these other identities. In all of these cases, we will be exploring how American definitions of race and ethnicity have shaped Jewish identity, and to what extent Jews can be considered "insiders" or "outsiders" in American life.) Monday Only Classes: Wednesday, December 9, 2026, will serve as the designated class meeting day for all Fall 2026 courses that are regularly scheduled to meet only on Mondays.
